existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Fees limited to actual cost of search, retrieval, and redaction
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The public body may establish and collect fees as provided for in this section. The public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67 revised fee structure)
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; city sets the operative fee under it. Note redaction time IS chargeable here, but exemption-review time is NOT (SC-0013) — the two are distinguished.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Search/retrieval/redaction labor rate capped at lowest-paid-qualified-employee salary
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The fee for search, retrieval, or redaction shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the custodian's reasonable discretion, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The fee for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling tied to a computed value (prorated hourly salary of lowest-paid qualified employee); city supplies the actual rate under the cap.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Copy fee capped at prevailing commercial rate
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling = prevailing commercial rate; no fixed per-page cents figure is set by statute (see material negatives).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Copy fees must be uniform for the same record
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Fees charged must be uniform for copies of the same record or document across requesters.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Split from SC-0009: a non-discrimination standard (uniformity) distinct from the commercial-rate ceiling, drawn from the same sentence.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No copy charge for records transmitted electronically
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Copy charges may not be applied to records that are transmitted in an electronic format.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Record is transmitted in electronic format
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Copy charges may not apply to records that are transmitted in an electronic format.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Fixed value of $0 for the copy-charge component when delivery is electronic. Search/retrieval/redaction labor may still be charged; only the per-copy charge is barred.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Charge permitted for converting non-electronic records to electronic format
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If records are not in electronic format and the public body agrees to produce them electronically, it may charge for the staff time required to transfer the documents to electronic format.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Records not in electronic format and public body agrees to produce electronically
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If records are not in electronic format and the public body agrees to produce them in electronic format, the public body may charge for the staff time required to transfer the documents to electronic format.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Chargeable amount is "staff time," bounded by the labor-rate cap (SC-0008); no separate rate is fixed. Conversion charge is an exception to the no-electronic-copy-charge rule (SC-0011).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No fee for examination/review to determine disclosability
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if documents are subject to disclosure.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Time spent reviewing records to determine disclosability
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if the documents are subject to disclosure.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Fixed $0 for exemption-review labor. Distinguish from redaction, which IS chargeable under SC-0007/SC-0008 — the boundary between reviewing-for-exemption (free) and redacting (chargeable) is a known human-review flag.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Records furnished at lowest possible cost
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting them.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Undefined standard ("lowest possible cost") governing how fees are computed; kept as a soft standard, not converted to a number.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver/reduction in the public interest
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may furnish documents without charge or at a reduced charge where it determines that waiver or reduction is in the public interest because furnishing the information primarily benefits the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Agency determination that furnishing primarily benefits the general public
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Documents may be furnished when appropriate without charge or at a reduced charge where the agency determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because furnishing the information can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Discretionary branch (waive / reduce / no waiver); the engine must be able to execute a fee-waiver decision path.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No charge to General Assembly members for legislative-duty requests
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Members of the General Assembly may receive copies of records or documents at no charge when the request relates to their legislative duties.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester is a member of the General Assembly and request relates to legislative duties
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: However, members of the General Assembly may receive copies of records or documents at no charge from public bodies when their request relates to their legislative duties.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Special-requester-class branch (fee = $0) conditioned on legislative-duty nexus.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Public body must post a fee schedule online
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall develop a fee schedule and post it online.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation governing fees charged on requests)
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The public body shall develop a fee schedule to be posted online.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Included because the fee applied to an individual request must come from a published schedule; borderline administrative, but directly binds the fee value used in processing.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Deposit up to 25% of anticipated reproduction cost before search/copying
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require, prior to searching for or making copies of records, a deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Before the public body searches for or copies records
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records may be required prior to the public body searching for or making copies of records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling = 25% of anticipated reproduction cost; city sets whether/how much deposit to require under the cap. When a deposit is required, the production clock runs from deposit receipt (SC-0026).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Full cost due at time of production
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Payment step gating release; balance beyond any deposit is collected at production.
